category_title: Students with ASD and profound hearing loss exhibiting escape-motivated tantrums during academic tasks
minimal_context: Charlie is sitting at a table in his classroom during reading class and is asked to read a paragraph from a book aloud.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Charlie, it is time for our reading lesson. Please look at this book and read the first paragraph aloud.

STUDENT: (Pushes the book away and shakes his head to refuse to work)

TUTOR: We need to do our reading work now. Please start reading.

STUDENT: (Starts to melt down, whining and engaging in avoidance behaviors by turning his body away from the reading material)

TUTOR: Charlie, you need to stay at the table and finish this assignment.

STUDENT: (Screams loudly, pounds his fist on the table, and leaves his chair to escape the reading work)

options.A: Creating a classroom reading community founded on respect for choice and individual perspectives, and maintaining this environment for the student consistently throughout the reading class.
options.B: Involving the student in developing and adjusting the reading assessment rubric early in the unit, and reviewing these expectations consistently throughout the reading class.
options.C: Analyzing the reading demand for possible reasons why the student is motivated to escape the work (e.g., excessively difficult work), and providing reinforcement for doing gradually increasing amounts of reading.
options.D: Varying reading instruction by including more active learning strategies, and incorporating cooperative learning groups for the student consistently throughout the reading class.
